## Source Map — GOV-003 / AMLO 2022 / Chapter 5B

**Document type:** financial_report (press release, SHCP). **Role:** executive_official_report — single ministry bulletin, narrative-driven, links to underlying statistics on the SHCP Presto portal.

### Atomic claims (with locators)

1. **Accounting period & framing.** Report covers cumulative close of 2022 ("cuarto año de la administración"); dated 30 January 2023 by SHCP. [Block 1]
2. **Headline debt-to-GDP.** Public debt = **49.4% of GDP**; reported as below the 2022 budget target by 1.6 pp of GDP and below 2021 by 1.4 pp of GDP. Attributed to "buen desempeño de los ingresos presupuestarios" net of the IEPS fuel subsidy; revenues exceeded budget by 1.5% of GDP. [Block 1]
3. **Growth narrative (caution).** Mexican economy grew **2.9% YoY through November 2022**, framed as "better than analysts expected." Incomplete-year figure (Jan–Nov), not full-year. [Block 2]
4. **Labour-market narrative (partial period).** Unemployment **2.8% overall / 2.5% for women**, framed as "lowest in 17 years"; 2.4 million jobs created in 2022, "mostly formal." [Block 2]
5. **Private consumption.** **7.1% cumulative growth through October 2022**, vs historical average 2.7%; services consumption recovered to pre-pandemic levels. [Block 2] **Caveat:** through-October, not full-year.
6. **FDI inflow.** **USD 32 bn through Q3 2022**; characterised as the highest since 2013. [Block 2] **Caveat:** nine-month figure.
7. **Global outlook (assertion).** Disruptions in supply chains and transport costs "decreased," easing inflationary pressure; analysts raised 2022 global growth; 2023 global growth seen at ~2.1%, helped by China reopening and lower commodity prices. [Block 2] **Role:** narrative forecast/assertion, no model shown.
8. **Capex narrative.** Gross fixed investment **+5.5% YoY through October** vs historical average 1.6%; machinery and equipment **+12.2% YoY** vs historical 5.0%. [Block 3] **Caveat:** through-October.
9. **IMSS formal jobs.** **753,000 new IMSS-affiliated jobs in 2022**, "third highest since 1997"; real average wage **+2.7% YoY**. **1.3 million IMSS jobs added** over Dec 2018–Dec 2022, "higher than for Calderón and Fox over the same period." [Block 3]
10. **Trade.** Foreign trade reached a "historical maximum" of **MXN 1.2 trillion (USD) in 2022**, driven by record manufacturing exports; new-investment FDI = **USD 14 bn**, "second-highest after 2013." Net capital outflows were **USD 19 bn lower than 2021**. [Block 3]
11. **Public revenues 2022 (full-year).** Total revenues = **MXN 6.595 trillion**, **MXN 422 bn above budget**; YoY real growth **2.5%**; two consecutive years of growth. Federal revenues exceeded budget by MXN 632 bn, of which **MXN 397 bn corresponds to lower IEPS-fuel-tax collection** (i.e., the stimulus cost). [Block 4]
12. **Oil revenues.** **MXN 1.482 trillion = 5.2% of GDP** — "highest since 2014"; real YoY **+18.7%**; attributed to high oil prices. [Block 4] **Role:** revenue line strongly commodity-driven.
13. **Tax administration.** Non-fuel-IEPS tax revenues = **13.6% of GDP**, "highest on record"; real YoY **+7.8%** ("highest rate since 2016"). [Block 4]
14. **ISR / IVA.** ISR = **MXN 2.270 trillion (8.0% of GDP)**, "historical maximum," real YoY **+11%** (highest since 2016). IVA = **MXN 1.222 trillion (4.3% of GDP)** vs historical avg 3.9%. [Block 4]
15. **Public spending 2022.** Total public spending = **MXN 7.569 trillion (26.5% of GDP)**; real YoY **+4.1%**; three consecutive years of growth. [Block 5]
16. **Composition.** Social-protection spending **+8.7% real**, 5.3% of GDP ("new historical max"). Physical investment **+25.2%** (highest since 2009), 3.3% of GDP ("highest since 2016"). Transfers to states/municipalities "largest since records exist," real YoY **+7.3%**. [Block 5]
17. **Fiscal balances (% of GDP).** Primary balance **deficit 0.5%**; public deficit **3.4%**; Public-Sector Financial Requirements (RFSP) **4.4%**. [Block 5] **Note:** all three presented without comparative period.
18. **Fiscal buffers.** Joint fiscal buffers = **USD 262 bn**: international reserves, IMF Flexible Credit Line, US Fed swap line, stabilization funds. [Block 5]
19. **Debt sustainability (assertion).** Public debt "at a sustainable level, lower than 2021," attributed to refinancing-cost reduction and lower FX/rate exposure. [Block 5]
20. **Q4 2022 debt operations.** 7 Oct: peso-denominated debt buyback of **MXN 68,017 m** (maturities 2023–2046), paired with long-term peso bond/Udibono sale of **MXN 48,596 m**. 30 Nov: 3rd Bondes G placement — MXN 7,090 m (1y), MXN 2,660 m (2y), MXN 250 m (3y). 7 Dec: new Bono M maturing May 2033, **MXN 12,500 m at 7.5% coupon**. 8 Dec: Bono M placements for 2033/2053 **MXN 50,863 m**, plus buyback of Bono M maturing 2029–2047. [Block 6]
21. **Debt-service smoothing (assertion).** "For 2023 and the next two years" debt-servicing pressure reduced **on average 73%** via buybacks, "freeing USD 3 bn for the next administration." [Block 6] **Note:** basis of the 73% computation not disclosed in extract.
22. **Reputation claims.** "21 international recognitions for debt-management strategy" over the four-year term; investment grade maintained with stable outlook from all 8 rating agencies. [Block 6]

### Observed facts vs. assertions vs. interpretation
- **Observed/numeric:** items 1, 2, 4, 5 (period-bounded), 6 (period-bounded), 8 (period-bounded), 9–17, 20.
- **Assertions / qualitative framing:** items 3 ("better than expected"), 7 (global inflation/disruptions narrative), 9 (comparative-sexenio claim), 10 ("historical maximum" trade), 18 (buffers framed as "blindaje"), 19 ("sustainable"), 21 (73% reduction), 22 (21 recognitions, 8/8 stable).
- **Interpretive:** attribution of debt decline to revenue performance (block 1); attribution of revenue strength to anti-evasion efforts (block 4); attribution of capex growth to "priorities of the administration" (block 5).

### Unresolved allegations / contrary material / limitations
- All growth, consumption, investment, FDI and trade series are **partial-year** (Oct or Nov 2022); full-year audited outturns not in extract.
- Debt reduction claimed vs 2021 (1.4 pp of GDP); extract gives 2022 debt ratio but not the 2021 ratio separately, nor FX/coverage basis.
- 73% debt-pressure reduction (item 21) lacks methodology, base year, and debt-service denominator; cannot verify from extract.
- "Evasión fiscal" gains (item 13) presented without counterfactual or measurement method.
- No statement on **contingent liabilities, SOE debt, pension liabilities, state/local balances, arrears, off-budget funds, or guarantee exposure**. Coverage appears limited to **Federal Government / RFSP** aggregates.
- No auditor's opinion, no revision history, no accrual-vs-cash note in extract; press-release form, not a financial statement with notes.
- Debt operations (item 20) reported only for Q4 2022 events; cumulative annual issuance/refinancing totals not disclosed.
- "21 international recognitions" and "8/8 stable outlook" (item 22) are unverifiable from the extract; names of recognitions and rating agencies not listed.
- Oil-revenue surge (item 12) materially tied to commodity prices, which the report itself cites; sustainability post-2022 not addressed.

### Sections a stronger model should reopen
1. **Debt-to-GDP cross-check** against later SHCP / Banxico / IMF Article IV figures to detect revisions and FX/coverage differences (only 2022 ratio given here, not 2021 baseline).
2. **Fiscal aggregates (3.4% deficit, RFSP 4.4%)** with explicit comparator year and consolidation perimeter.
3. **Revenue over-performance decomposition** (item 11): separate oil-driven from non-oil; quantify the MXN 397 bn IEPS-fuel stimulus cost as a fiscal cost vs revenue offset.
4. **73% debt-pressure claim** (item 21): re-derive from scheduled amortisation profile and refinancing spreads.
5. **Investment-growth figures** (items 8, 16): convert from through-October to full-year; reconcile 25.2% physical-investment growth with 12.2% machinery growth for consistency.
6. **Coverage gaps** noted above (SOEs, pensions, states, contingent liabilities).
7. **21 recognitions and rating-agency count** (item 22) — verify against the cited primary sources.

### Continuation flag
Material content fits within target length; no explicit continuation emitted. Source role, traps and reading-brief caveats fully applied to items above.
